shangguan_day_branch.defline: The Virtuoso lives inside your Day Gate, the seat of your partner: your closest bond runs on talk, wit and honesty.
shangguan_day_branch.reading: You want a partner quick enough to argue with and warm enough to praise you, and you lose interest in anyone who only agrees. Because being understood is how you feel loved, you say exactly what you notice at home, and the sharpest of it lands on the person you care about most. Your best ideas get worked out in those arguments, and you think more clearly beside someone who pushes back than on your own.

Love.headline: You love the person who can answer you back.
Love.recognition: You show love by talking and teasing, and a quiet partner leaves you lonely even in a happy home. Since you feel close only when your mind is met, you keep testing your partner with argument, and some evenings end colder than either of you meant. What you want is praise and honesty in the same person, and you rarely settle for half.
Love.lived: The partners you have chosen so far were quick ones, people who argued well and laughed at the right moments. More than once a relationship cooled because your honesty arrived before your warmth, and you remember which words did it.
Love.ahead: From your mid-thirties your home fills with talk, and the partner you share it with matches you word for word. The two of you grow closer through what you argue about together, and you aim your sharpest words at the world outside your door.

Mind.headline: Your mind is sharpest in conversation with someone close.
Mind.recognition: You think best out loud, with one person close enough to hear the rough version and sharp enough to push back. Because your ideas only feel real once they have been tested on someone, an evening of silence at home leaves you restless. You give your partner your best ideas first, and your harshest opinions too.
Mind.lived: Your clearest thinking so far has happened in long talks with someone close, more than in study or alone at a desk. You have changed your mind more than once because a partner disagreed, and you have also argued long after either of you was listening.
Mind.ahead: Your thinking grows bolder from your mid-thirties, and a partner is the first to hear each new idea. The ideas the two of you test at home in these years become the ones you are known for, and you say them more kindly than you once did.

shangguan_hour_branch.defline: The Virtuoso lives inside your Hour Gate: your later life stays full of ideas, opinions and people who argue back.
shangguan_hour_branch.reading: In later life you keep making things and saying what you think, and you look for younger people who will answer you back. Because being heard has always kept you well, the ones who stand up to you become your favourites, whether they are children or younger relatives or someone you train. Your family gets your sharpest wit and your newest plans, and you stay closest to the ones who also get your warmth.

Family.headline: Your family stays loud with argument and ideas.
Family.recognition: You love your family through talk, about ideas and plans and whatever they are getting wrong. Because a good argument is how you stay close, you push the people you love harder than strangers, and the gentler ones keep their distance. What you want from your family is a table that talks back, and the weeks it goes quiet are the ones you like least.
Family.lived: The talk in your family has got sharper and funnier since your late forties, with younger people answering you back. You have been proudest when one of them beat you in an argument, and you have rarely said so.
Family.ahead: From your late forties the people after you seek you out for talk they cannot get anywhere else. You become the one in your family whose opinion is asked for, and you give it with more warmth than you once did.

Mind.headline: Your mind stays quick and restless with every decade.
Mind.recognition: You keep your mind busy with projects and opinions, and an empty week wears you down faster than a hard one. Since an idea feels finished to you only once it has been argued, you go looking for a debate when none comes to you. Your thinking stays quick while it has work, and you feel the loss within days when it has none.
Mind.lived: Your mind has kept finding new work since your late forties, a subject or a project picked up whenever an old one ran out. You have started more debates in this stretch than in any earlier decade, and you have enjoyed nearly all of them.
Mind.ahead: Your thinking gets bolder past your late forties, and you say plainly what you held back in earlier years. An idea that grips you keeps you up at night, and you sleep well again once you have said it out loud.

shangguan_hour_stem.defline: The Virtuoso stands at your Hour Gate, in plain view: your later years are when people hear you most clearly.
shangguan_hour_stem.reading: In later life you do your boldest work, at a point when most people expect you to ease off. Because saying the true thing matters more to you than a title, you speak more freely each year, and some who hold rank resent it. You keep changing while there is something new to learn. You pass your talent to the people after you, children or younger relatives or someone you train, along with your dislike of being told what to do.

Career.headline: Your best work is the work you do last.
Career.recognition: You do your best work where you can say what you think, and a job that asks for quiet manners tires you. Because your skill has grown faster than your patience for rules, you are better at the job than many who manage it. What you make in later life outlasts the job that paid for it, and you judge yourself by the work alone.
Career.lived: Your work has grown bolder since your late forties, and you have said things in public that you once kept back. At least once a role ended because you would not soften a view, and you did better work in the next one.
Career.ahead: From your late forties your influence grows as titles start to matter less, and people begin to repeat what you say. Younger people carry your methods into their own work, and you hear your own style in the way they argue with you.

Growth.headline: You grow for as long as the work stays new.
Growth.recognition: You grow fastest when the task is new to you, a different kind of audience or a skill nobody expects you to take up. Because sameness bores you before it tires you, you leave a settled position sooner than others think wise. Each change costs you some comfort, and you come out of it sharper than you went in.
Growth.lived: Past your late forties you have changed direction more than once where others expected you to settle, taking up a new field or a new way of working. Each move looked risky to the people around you, and you grew more for it than in the calmer years before.
Growth.ahead: Saying out loud what you used to keep to yourself becomes your way of growing from your late forties, and people who once called you difficult start calling you wise. You stay sharp in these years while something in your life is new, and you go looking for it when nothing is.

shangguan_month_branch.defline: The Virtuoso holds your strongest seat, inside your Month Gate: your working years run on seeing how everything could be better.
shangguan_month_branch.reading: You spot the better version of a plan, a process or a piece of work almost at once, and the weaker version nags at you for days. Because an unfixed flaw weighs on you more than hard work does, you keep improving things long after others call them finished, and you are still thinking about them at night. Managers find you tiring and colleagues find you useful, and you are proud of being both.

Career.headline: You are paid to make things better.
Career.recognition: You are best in jobs where improving things is the work itself, editing or design or reform of some kind. Because a weak plan is plain to you before anyone asks, you correct work that was never yours to correct. Your value at work grows with every process you improve, and you are known as the colleague who will not let poor work pass.
Career.lived: In class, in teams and in your first jobs you have been the one who points out what could be better. You have clashed with at least one boss over it, and you have also been the person they sent for when something needed fixing.

Mind.headline: Your mind never stops improving what it sees.
Mind.recognition: You think in revisions, turning over a plan or an idea or your own opinion until it is better, and nothing feels quite finished to you. Since a fault you have noticed stays with you until it is mended, your mind keeps working when the day is over. You sleep best in the weeks when one hard problem has all of your attention.
Mind.lived: Your mind has gone looking for faults since your late teens, in what you were taught and in what you believed yourself. You have changed your view on something important more than once over those years, and each time you argued yourself into the new view first.

shangguan_month_stem.defline: The Virtuoso stands at your Month Gate, in plain view: at work and among friends you are seen as gifted and hard to manage.
shangguan_month_stem.reading: Your talent is the first thing colleagues see, and your patience with rules is the last. Because you need your work to be judged fairly, you shine under bosses who reward results and stall under bosses who want obedience. Your friends are the people who enjoy your sharpest remarks, and you have lost a few who did not. You have walked away from at least one job that wanted you quieter.

Career.headline: You are hired for your talent and tested on your discipline.
Career.recognition: You do your strongest work where you can be seen doing it, pitching or teaching or leading from the front. Because you need honest credit to stay interested, a desk job under close supervision drains you within months. Your talent wins you the role, and your record of finishing decides how long you keep it.
Career.lived: Bosses have either backed you fully or tried to slow you down since your late teens, and few have stayed neutral about you. You have done your best work for the ones who believed in you, and you have outlasted most of the ones who did not.

Social.headline: Friends and colleagues either love you or resist you.
Social.recognition: Your circle splits quickly into people who champion you and people who resent you, with few in between. Because being remembered matters more to you than being liked, you say the sharp thing in company and lose a friend or two to it. Your loyal few have done more for your name than general approval could, and you keep them close for years.
Social.lived: Your friendships since your late teens have formed around strong reactions, people who liked your edge at once or never warmed to it. More than once a friendship ended over something you said in public, and you have kept every friend who stayed through it.

shangguan_year_branch.defline: The Virtuoso lives inside your Year Gate: underneath your childhood ran a quiet disagreement with the way things were done at home.
shangguan_year_branch.reading: You asked why before most children do, and the habit of doubting first has stayed with you. Because you learned early to trust your own judgement over what you were told, you have grown fastest in places that let you test things for yourself. Some in your family took your honesty for defiance, and you are closest now to the relatives who heard you out.

Family.headline: Your family gets your honesty along with your love.
Family.recognition: You love your family most easily where you are allowed to disagree, and a home that asks you to keep quiet feels cold to you. Because honesty was your first way of belonging at home, you say what others leave unsaid, and a relative or two finds you hard work. Your warmth is real, and you show it most to the people who argue back.
Family.lived: You questioned at least one rule in your first home that everyone else accepted, quietly or out loud. Someone there found you difficult for it, and by your teens you had learned which opinions to keep to yourself.

Growth.headline: You grow by doubting what you are given.
Growth.recognition: You improve anything you are handed by questioning it first, a method or a belief or a piece of advice. Since accepting things whole has never felt honest to you, you learn more slowly from teachers and faster from your own mistakes. Your doubt turns into skill whenever it has real work in front of it, and you grow restless when it has none.
Growth.lived: You had outgrown some of what your family believed by your teens, and you got there by arguing with it. In school you did best in the subjects that let you question the answer, and you drifted through the ones that did not.

shangguan_year_stem.defline: The Virtuoso stands at your Year Gate, in plain view: you were known early as the bright child who answered back.
shangguan_year_stem.reading: In class you spotted the flaw in a lesson and said so before the teacher had finished. Because your mind moves faster than others expect, the company you keep sorts quickly into those who enjoy you and those who resent you. Teachers and older relatives were the first to feel both reactions, and you have done better each time you picked your own friends and your own work.

Social.headline: People remember you after one meeting.
Social.recognition: You get noticed in any group, for a quick remark or an opinion nobody else would voice. Because being seen as bright has been part of you since childhood, you feel flat in company that only wants small talk. The friends who enjoy your sharpness stay for years, and you lose interest in the ones who only tolerate it.
Social.lived: As a child your remarks were the ones repeated at family gatherings and at the school gate. By your teens you had a few friends who loved your wit and a teacher or two who had given up on you.

Mind.headline: Your mind gets there first and gets bored first.
Mind.recognition: You see the pattern before others have finished explaining it, and boredom reaches you long before the lesson ends. Since your thinking was praised early for speed, you are careless with the slower parts of a problem. Your mind does its best work on hard problems with someone watching, and you drift when it has neither.
Mind.lived: You finished the work early at school and went looking for something harder, or for trouble when nothing harder came. Before you left school you had taught yourself at least one subject well beyond your class, and you had learned to hide how bored you were.

shishen_day_branch.defline: The Artisan lives inside your Day Gate, the seat of your partner: your private life is built around comfort shared at home.
shishen_day_branch.reading: You are happiest where food, rest and easy company are part of every day, and you choose a partner who enjoys them with you. Because ease makes you feel safe, you look after the people you live with through meals and small favours more than through words. Your relatives and friends end up at your table, and you give so much to the household that your own rest comes last.

Love.headline: You show love by making life easy.
Love.recognition: You love by doing, the meal made and the evening kept free and the worry taken off someone's hands. Since giving comfort is how you feel close, you feel most loved by a partner who receives it gladly and gives some back. You give without keeping count, and you notice a partner who only takes much later than your friends do.
Love.lived: The relationships that have lasted for you so far were the gentle ones, with partners who liked a quiet evening as much as you did. At least once you cooked and cared for someone who gave little back, and you stayed longer than the relationship deserved.
Love.ahead: From your mid-thirties your love life settles into a shared home with a partner who makes ordinary days pleasant. The two of you build your life around the same table, and you find yourself looked after in return more than at any time before.

Family.headline: You become the host your family returns to.
Family.recognition: Your home is where your family ends up, for meals and holidays and the nights someone needs a bed. Because a full house makes you feel settled, you take on more hosting than anyone asks of you. Relatives treat your door as always open, and you rarely show them how tired you are by the end.
Family.lived: Wherever you have lived so far, people have drifted to your kitchen for a meal or a night or a long weekend. You have fed more people than you could easily afford to, and you have counted it as time well spent.
Family.ahead: Your house becomes the place your family gathers once you are past your mid-thirties, and relatives and friends treat it as a second home. Quarrels in the family get settled over your meals, and you become the relative everyone means when they say home.

Health.headline: Your body does well when home is calm.
Health.recognition: Your health follows your home life closely, and you sleep and eat well in the seasons when the house is peaceful. Because tension at home reaches your body before you name it, a bad month with a partner shows up in your appetite and your rest. You recover fastest through ordinary comfort, a shared meal and an early night.
Health.lived: Your energy has risen and fallen so far with the state of your home, steady in the good years and low in the strained ones. Your sleep and appetite have followed each change at home, and they have settled again whenever the house grew calm.
Health.ahead: Your sleep and appetite steady from your mid-thirties as your household settles, and a calm year at home gives you more energy than a busy one. In the fullest of these years you eat and rest in step with whoever shares your home, and you stay well because of it.

shishen_hour_branch.defline: The Artisan lives inside your Hour Gate: your later life settles into good food, deep sleep and people who keep coming back.
shishen_hour_branch.reading: In later life you get to enjoy the comfort you have worked for, and your home fills with younger people and long friendships. Because care has always meant a good meal and a warm bed to you, you keep feeding whoever comes, whether they are children or younger relatives or someone you train. Ease is both the reward of those years and their one risk, and you stay well for as long as your days keep a rhythm.

Family.headline: Your later family is the people at your table.
Family.recognition: You treat anyone who eats at your home often enough as family, and a friend who comes every week matters to you as much as a cousin. Because feeding people is how you show care, you keep inviting people long after others have stopped hosting. Your house stays busy because of it, and you would feel lost in a home that no one visits.
Family.lived: Your home has filled with the people after you since your late forties, and with friends who come for the food. You have hosted more in this stretch than in any earlier decade, and you have started to be fed by the people you once fed.
Family.ahead: From your late forties the people after you gather at your table more each year. The care you have given starts to come back to you in these years, and you are looked after by those you once fed.

Health.headline: Your body grows easier to live in each decade.
Health.recognition: You look after your body through regular meals, gentle movement and people nearby, and it answers you well. Since rest comes easily to you, a good week of it stretches into a slow month before you notice. Your health depends more on company than on effort, and you feel the difference within days when you eat alone.
Health.lived: Your sleep has deepened since your late forties and your appetite has steadied, and you have enjoyed your food more than ever. Your energy has dipped in the stretches when you were on your own too much, and it has come back each time the house filled up again.
Health.ahead: Your body settles into an easy routine from your late forties, with good sleep and steady appetite and company at meals. These years suit your body unusually well, and you stay strong in them while there are people around you.

shishen_hour_stem.defline: The Artisan stands at your Hour Gate, in plain view: your later years are known for what you make and give.
shishen_hour_stem.reading: In later life people see you cooking, mending or teaching for others, and children or younger relatives or someone you train pick up your skills along with your generosity. Because being useful puts you at ease, you keep making things for the pleasure of it and passing on what your hands know. Comfort that asks nothing of you is the one thing that slows your work, and you notice it in the weeks with no one to make anything for.

Family.headline: You become the relative everyone wants to visit.
Family.recognition: In your family you are the one who remembers birthdays, cooks for the holidays and never arrives empty-handed. Because giving is how you feel close, you hand over gifts more easily than advice. Your family takes after your kindness more than your opinions, and you are glad of the trade.
Family.lived: You have become the relative who hosts since your late forties, the one whose home younger people head for at holidays. The people after you have picked up your habits of giving, and you see yourself in how they treat their own guests.
Family.ahead: From your late forties your family gathers around what you give, the meals and the gifts and the time. Younger people grow easy and generous around you, and you see the best of yourself in them.

Career.headline: Your later work is your most generous.
Career.recognition: You work best on things that feed people in some way, a meal or a lesson or a well-made thing. Because making something well gives you more pleasure than any title, you turn down promotions that would take you away from the work itself. Your work runs on pleasure, and you do more of it in a happy month than in a pressured year.
Career.lived: Your work has turned since your late forties toward teaching, hosting or finishing projects you had put off for years. Some of what you have made in this stretch has been better received than anything from your busier decades, and you have been surprised by it.
Career.ahead: Your working life turns productive in the ways that suit you from your late forties, through mentoring and making and work done for others. You do some of your best work in these years, and you are paid for it in thanks as well as money.

shishen_month_branch.defline: The Artisan holds your strongest seat, inside your Month Gate: your working years run on steady craft and a body kept well.
shishen_month_branch.reading: You do your work steadily and without fuss, and over the years you quietly produce more than people who make more noise. Because your energy comes from sleep, food and routine, your work rises and falls with how well you are living. You do your best in making, feeding or teaching, and you keep improving at it long after others have peaked.

Career.headline: Your career runs on craft and good habits.
Career.recognition: Your best work comes from skill built slowly, in fields where the hands or the senses know things. Since steady practice is what you trust, you are slow to take on work you cannot yet do well, and you miss a few openings that way. You are seldom the loudest on a team, and your work is the work that holds up.
Career.lived: You have built your skill quietly since your late teens, through practice more than ambition, in work that let you make or tend something. In time the people around you came to call your skill a gift, and you knew it had come one day at a time.

Health.headline: Your work is only as good as your sleep.
Health.recognition: Your body and your work move together, and both run best on regular meals, real rest and a steady routine. Because food and rest are pleasures to you, you eat late and sleep short in busy months, and your energy drops. You notice tiredness in your work before you feel it, and a few good nights put it right.
Health.lived: Your energy has followed your routine closely since your late teens, high in the months you slept and ate well and flat when either slipped. At least once a long stretch of hard work wore you down, and you came back from it through rest more than effort.

shishen_month_stem.defline: The Artisan stands at your Month Gate, in plain view: at work and among friends you are known as the easy, gifted maker.
shishen_month_stem.reading: Much of what you produce looks effortless to the people around you, and most of it is simply work you enjoy. Because enjoyment is what drives you, the jobs you like go well for you and the ones you only endure stall. Colleagues and friends find you easy company, and that ease has brought you more openings than ambition has. You coast through a smooth year without noticing, and you feel the cost only when it ends.

Career.headline: You earn most from the work you enjoy.
Career.recognition: Your best work comes when you like it, and everyone around you can tell the difference within a week. Since pleasure is what keeps you going, a joyless job empties you out faster than a demanding one. Your ease makes you look less ambitious than you are, and you let the finished work speak for you.
Career.lived: Through your first working years your best jobs were the ones you enjoyed, and your worst stretches went on forcing yourself through work you disliked. At least once a parent or an older colleague took your ease for a lack of drive, and you proved them wrong quietly.

Social.headline: Your easy manner wins you friends at work.
Social.recognition: You put people at ease without trying, and a tense meeting turns friendly once you join it. Because sharing food and good company is how you connect, much of your working circle began over a lunch or a drink. You know more people than you realise, and you are slow to ask any of them for a favour.
Social.lived: Your closest friends at work since your late teens have come out of shared breaks and long evenings, the colleagues you ate with. More than once a friendly contact has turned into a job or an opening, and you had not been looking for either.

shishen_year_branch.defline: The Artisan lives inside your Year Gate: underneath your early years were comfort and care, given freely.
shishen_year_branch.reading: As a child you were fed well, in more than one sense, and that early comfort still sits under the way you live. Because ease was given to you before you had to earn it, you recover through simple things, food and a full night's sleep and the company of people you love. Whatever else your first home held, you took from it a store of warmth you have drawn on in every hard season since.

Family.headline: You were fed well, and you became the one who feeds.
Family.recognition: You hold your family together through comfort, the visit kept and the favour done and the table set. Because care reached you first as warmth, you give it back the same way, and you feel useless in a family crisis that kindness cannot touch. What you want from your family is ease, and you work hard to make it.
Family.lived: Someone in your early life made comfort a daily thing, often an older relative who gave without being asked. You still judge a home by how it feels to walk into, and you have made yours warmer than the ones you grew up beside.

Health.headline: Your body trusts food and rest to put it right.
Health.recognition: You trust your body to fix itself with a good meal and a long sleep, and for most of your life it has. Because comfort is how you recover, you reach for it under stress, and you turn the extra helping or the lost weekend into a habit before you notice. Your body asks you for rhythm more than for effort.
Health.lived: You were a child who recovered quickly, from colds and falls and bad days alike. Your appetite and your sleep were steady, and you came into adulthood with more reserve than most of the people around you.

shishen_year_stem.defline: The Artisan stands at your Year Gate, in plain view: warmth and easy charm were the first things people saw in you.
shishen_year_stem.reading: Affection reached you early and without effort, from the older relatives around you and from children you had only just met. Because being liked came so easily, you expect a welcome wherever you go, and you usually get one. Your body has run well on regular meals and sleep, and you feel the cost of too many late nights later than your friends do.

Social.headline: You are welcomed in almost any company.
Social.recognition: People warm to you on first meeting, and they remember how you made them feel long after the talk itself. Since being liked was your first way of belonging, you give more than you take in every circle you join, through hosting and small kindnesses. Your friends are many and loyal, and you show your worries to very few of them.
Social.lived: Other children wanted to sit next to you, and the adults at family gatherings made a fuss of you. By your teens you were asked to more parties than you could go to, and you went to most of them.

Health.headline: You were born with a forgiving body.
Health.recognition: You recover quickly from big meals and short nights, and your body has rarely let you down. Because pleasure has never felt dangerous to you, you let the treats and the late nights pile up until your energy drops. A steady routine of food and rest puts you right, and you feel well again within a week of going back to it.
Health.lived: You ate well and slept soundly in your first years, and a bad day or a cold never kept you down for long. Food at home was a pleasure more than a rule, and by your teens you loved a good meal more than most of your friends did.
